goals: Create an in-game accessible personal notebook for Minecraft Java 26.2 Fabric where players can write, edit, organize, and revisit notes without an external text editor.
Keep the eventual experience lightweight, predictable, Minecraft-native, and vanilla-plus rather than turning it into a complex document editor.
scope: Choose an appropriate in-game interaction or keybind for opening and closing the notebook after inspecting the current Minecraft and Fabric APIs.
Persist player-authored text across save/reload and normal game or server restarts.
Provide multiple notes, pages, or another deliberately simple organizational model.
Support creating, renaming, editing, and deleting notes.
Define predictable notebook ownership and persistence behavior across dimension changes and player death.
Provide a clean Minecraft-native user interface suitable for a lightweight vanilla-plus utility.
Handle formatting input, long notes, unusual and Unicode characters, and empty notes safely.
Decide detailed user experience and storage architecture only when implementation begins and current Minecraft Java 26.2 and Fabric APIs have been inspected.

exclusions: Implementation source, placeholder Java, build files, speculative scaffolding, generated assets, Canary versions, artifacts, deployment, and runtime testing during project initialization.
A fixed opening interaction, keybind, page model, text-formatting model, client/server responsibility split, or persistence architecture before current Minecraft and Fabric APIs are inspected.
Complex document-editor features beyond the approved lightweight vanilla-plus notebook goal unless separately prioritized later.
Changes to another project, originals, shared runtime state, either Minecraft instance, or unrelated Workbench infrastructure.
Dependencies on other Workbench projects or third-party systems unless implementation evidence later establishes a real need.

state.milestone: Official Notebook project initialized; architecture, implementation, artifacts, and runtime work have not started.
